provenance: Real GPU runs on AMD MI355X (ROCm). PRISM-trained ORBIT-2 applied to independent Open-Meteo ERA5 data for Washington DC — a true out-of-distribution test. GHSL built-up surface (EU JRC) supplies the urban physics. Every number and map is measured, not synthesized.
task: 4x downscaling of 2m max temperature — July 4 2026 — Independence Day Heatwave (Open-Meteo ERA5, OOD)
test_split: Open-Meteo ERA5 DC heatwave — never seen in training (true OOD)

acts.title: Pretrained ORBIT-2
acts.text: ORBIT-2 8M is a vision foundation model pretrained on broad PRISM daily-weather data across the continental US (4x super-resolution). Here it is applied, with no tuning, to independent Open-Meteo ERA5 data for the DC heatwave — data it never saw.
acts.detail: Out of the box on the real Open-Meteo DC field: tmax MAE 3.658C.

acts.title: Out-of-distribution gap
acts.text: On this independent dataset the pretrained model does not beat a simple bilinear baseline. An honest out-of-distribution gap: a broadly-trained model is not automatically good on a new data source — and a smooth heatwave field is easy to interpolate.

acts.title: Finetuning alone plateaus
acts.text: We finetune on 814 real DC-region heatwave days mined from 37 years of PRISM (DC-window peak >= 35C). The model learns the heatwave regime and improves — but on truly out-of-distribution data it PLATEAUS: it still does not beat bilinear, and training further only overfits PRISM and diverges on Open-Meteo. Data-driven finetuning alone is not sufficient for true OOD.
acts.detail: DC tmax MAE 2.862C (21.8% better than pretrained) but still above bilinear 2.259C; urban-core 2.473C vs bilinear 1.683C.

acts.title: Physics conditioning breaks the plateau
acts.text: Bilinear interpolation has no physics — it cannot know where the concrete is. We condition the model on real GHSL built-up-surface density (EU JRC), the 'concrete jungle' signal, swapped into its land-cover channel. This injects physics that finetuning alone could not reach: the model sharpens the hot urban core, cutting the urban-core error 17.2% below the pure finetune.
acts.detail: Urban-core MAE 2.473C -> 2.047C (17.2% better than finetune alone); whole-window 2.594C. The gain is concentrated where the physics lives.

acts.title: The model learned the physics
acts.text: As a check we add an explicit urban-heat-island equation, T = T_model + beta * (urban_fraction - mean), calibrated from the measured DC heat signal. It adds essentially nothing on top of the conditioned model — confirming the model has already INTERNALIZED the urban physics from the conditioning field, rather than needing it bolted on afterward. Physics-in beats physics-on-top.
acts.detail: Urban-core MAE 2.047C (analytic UHI adds 0.0C — negligible; the conditioned model already captures ~100% of the core signal).
